title: Switzerland Has Lost Nearly a Fifth of Its Glacier Ice in Five Years
summary: Switzerland's glaciers are shrinking fast, and 2026 was another hard year for them. The Swiss Academy of Sciences, using GLAMOS glacier observations, reports the glaciers lost more than 5 percent of their ice volume in 2026. That did not quite match the record losses of 2022, but glaciers thinned by 2.5 to 4 meters on average, and by as much as 10 meters in some lower areas. Major glaciers including the Rhône, Aletsch, and Clariden had their most severe melting on record in 2026. Bella Tola in Valais and Griessfirn in Glarus have disappeared. Over five years, Switzerland has lost nearly 20 percent of its glacier ice. The winter of 2025 to 2026 was among Switzerland's ten least snowy winters, and heat and dry weather from May to September 2026 sped up melting. On 76 days, the freezing level climbed above 4,000 meters, a new Swiss record. From July to September, glaciers released about 2.2 trillion liters of water, easing summer water shortages. But scientists warn this help cannot last, because shrinking glaciers will provide less meltwater in the future.
why_it_matters: Meltwater from glaciers helps with summer water shortages, so losing glaciers matters for water everyone uses.
